title: Rust Host Agent cutover requires complete behavior parity evidence
claim: No Rust slice may receive production traffic or justify Go retirement until a provenance-bound manifest passes every CLI, schema/catalog, auth, MCP wire, provider, plan, durable-state, package, client, and isolated external-effect parity gate for the selected current Go revision. Missing, stale, malformed, or blocked evidence fails the gate. Cutover and Go retirement are separate decisions.
owner: The new host-agent Rust repository owns the parity manifest and verifier; the Host Agent, Platform, release, and deployment owners retain their respective cutover decisions.
rationale: A compiled binary, green unit tests, a health response, or a static tool list cannot establish that the replacement preserves an authenticated operational boundary or existing durable work.

included: all Host Agent modes, public capabilities, and configured provider projections
MCP, CLI, package, installation, and client behavior
plans, operations, observations, state conversion, and rollback
production cutover and subsequent Go retirement
excluded: new product capabilities, which require a separate OpenSpec delta
private deployment credentials and controller implementation

exception: No implicit exception. A different product contract requires a separately reviewed specification and owner decision. A blocked live test remains unverified and cannot be waived by a passing lower-level test.

required: exact Go source tree and current selected release/catalog revision
machine-readable parity inventory with supported modes and provider fixtures
differential CLI, schema/catalog, auth, and MCP wire results
provider lifecycle, Tasks/cancellation, plan, and durable-state results
isolated external-effect and rollback rehearsal results
published package and real client first-success results
Host Agent, Platform, release, and deployment owner cutover review
evidence.verifier: tools/parity/parity/verify.py (fail closed; negative tests in tools/parity/tests/test_verify.py)

revisionBehavior: A Go contract, package, mode, provider, schema, catalog, or transport revision change invalidates affected parity evidence and requires a reviewed source-lock and manifest rebase. A Rust implementation change reruns the affected gates and the whole-agent cutover verifier.

anchors.note: Pinned initial Go source and release/catalog provenance
Observable parity baseline and cutover requirement
Gates, evidence suites and one item per scenario

verificationStatus: Verifier implemented and fail closed. `make parity-verify-cutover` currently FAILS, as intended: it requires an inventory with no gaps (`requireNoGaps`), and owned gaps with no covering scenario remain, so passing every existing scenario is not enough. The M0 gate (`make parity-verify`) checks harness self-validation, canaries and inventory. Owner review of this invariant (task 0.5) is still pending, so status stays proposed.
